# BTOON

> BTOON ("Binary TOON") is a compact binary serialization format: MessagePack plus a columnar ("tabular") encoding for arrays of uniform objects, extension types (timestamp, date, datetime, bigint, float32/float64 vectors), an optional compression envelope and an optional HMAC-SHA256 signed envelope. Encoding is canonical (one value, one byte sequence, in every language) and decoders are hardened for hostile input. Spec version 0.1; libraries 0.1.x.

Key facts:

- Every BTOON document is valid MessagePack. BTOON's own types use negative extension ids: -1 timestamp, -2 date, -3 datetime, -4 bigint, -5 float32 vector, -6 float64 vector, -10 tabular. Generic MessagePack decoders see them as opaque extensions. With tabular encoding off, output is plain canonical MessagePack.
- Tabular encoding writes each key of an array of uniform maps once, then each column's values. Encoders use it only when a fixed size rule says it is smaller, so all implementations agree. Typical saving on record-shaped data: 35-45% versus MessagePack before compression.
- Canonical rules: smallest integer form by value, floats always float64 (NaN as 7ff8000000000000), map keys sorted by UTF-8 bytes, smallest headers, no trailing bytes.
- Decoders reject invalid UTF-8, duplicate keys, trailing bytes and non-string keys (strict mode, the default), limit nesting to 128, never allocate more than the input justifies, and cap decompression (256 MiB by default). Errors have stable codes such as truncated, invalid_utf8, duplicate_key, max_depth, invalid_tabular, invalid_envelope, size_limit, authentication_failed.
- Compression envelope: "BTON" magic, 16-byte header, zlib (required), LZ4, Zstandard, Brotli or Snappy. Signed envelope: "BTSG" magic, HMAC-SHA256 over header and payload, verified before parsing. Layering: sign(compress(encode(value))).
- BTOON borrows TOON's idea of writing table field names once. It is not a binary encoding of TOON text and is meant for storage and transport between programs, not for LLM prompts.

## Specification

- [SPEC.md](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-core/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md): the authoritative format specification (version 0.1)
- [Conformance vectors](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-core/tree/main/tests/vectors): test cases every implementation must pass
- [Implementation guide](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-core/blob/main/docs/IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md): notes for writing a new implementation

## Libraries

Released 2026-11-07 on every registry (0.1.x): `npm install @btoon/js` (pure TypeScript, recommended for JavaScript), `npm install btoon` (native Node.js addon), `pip install btoon`, `go get github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-go@v0.1.0`, `composer require btoon/btoon`, and the btoon CLI on the btoon-core GitHub release. The 0.0.x releases used an incompatible format.

- [btoon-core](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-core): C++20 reference implementation and the btoon CLI
- [btoon-python](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-python): Python bindings over the core, PyPI package btoon
- [btoon-nodejs](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-nodejs): Node.js native addon over the core, npm package btoon
- [btoon-javascript](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-javascript): pure TypeScript for browsers, Node.js, Deno, Bun and edge runtimes, npm package @btoon/js
- [btoon-go](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-go): pure Go, module github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-go
- [btoon-php](https://github.com/BTOON-project/btoon-php): pure PHP, Composer package btoon/btoon

## Website

- [Documentation](https://btoon.net/docs): overview, API options, error codes and format summary
- [Playground](https://btoon.net/docs#playground): encode JSON and decode BTOON in the browser
- [Benchmarks](https://btoon.net/benchmarks): published size and speed measurements, plus a benchmark that runs in the browser
- [Downloads](https://btoon.net/downloads): install and build instructions for each library
